title.narrative: Financial Guarantee -Mibanco Colombia - Microcredits for rural sector -2019-2025
Financial Guarantee -Mibanco Colombia - Microcredits for rural sector -2019-2025

description.narrative: Denna insats syftar till att använda lån och garantier som ett instrument för privatsektorsamarbete för rural utveckling
This contribution aims at starting the use of loans and guarantees as instrument for private sector collaboration, directed towards rural development.

This contribution aims to facilitate loans and financial services to micro-, small- and medium-sized rural and urban-based enterprises, women-owned businesses, and targeted beneficiary populations (Colombian victims of the conflict, ex-combatants in the process of reintegration, people with disabilities, Afro Colombian and Indigenous peoples) in rural regions that have been especially affected by armed conflict and thereby have no or little access to financial services.

The guarantee aimed to mobilize private capital and increase financing opportunities for micro-enterprises facing greater barriers, particularly women, in rural areas, and in priority territories affected by conflict.
Operating between December 2018 and May 2023, the program backed 15,544 loans totaling approximately 48.6 billion pesos (around US$12 million). This guarantee was evaluated between August and December 2025. The inception report of the evaluation showed that Mibanco's loan portfolio is composed of 82% unsecured or unspecified collateral loans. The National Guarantee Fund (FNG) represents 15%, followed by the USAID guarantee at 1.2%. The Sida´s guarantee accounts for 0.4%.
The main conclusion of the external evaluation was that the guarantee was effective in enabling people in vulnerable areas to access credit who would otherwise not have had this opportunity. There was a nearly 19% increase in the amounts disbursed, as well as a 26% increase in the number of loans in the municipalities where the program operated. Another positive outcome was that it succeeded in replacing loan sharks. In several territories, interviewees noted that access to guaranteed formal credit enabled beneficiaries to abandon costly and risky forms of financing.
The target of granting at least 54% of loans to women was not achieved in terms of either the number of loans or the amount disbursed, but the guarantee covered 52% which reflects the bank portfolio. The use of the Asdi guarantee was particularly limited in the priority areas designated under the PDET framework, which are defined as municipalities that were severely affected by the armed conflict and are central to the implementation of the Peace Agreement. Of the 45 PDET municipalities initially targeted, loans backed by the guarantee were issued in only 21 (46%).
There have been seven claims since the first payment in 2020. Below is a list of each claim, the number of individual claimed loans and date of payment: #1 93 sep 2020 #2 473 may 2022 #3 923 oct 2022 #4 622 abr 2023 #5 247 oct 2023 #6 558 nov 2024 #7 93 jun 2025 The total value for the seven claims paid out was 9 577 375 SEK, an amount subsequently decreased by recovery payments paid in by Mibanco.
